title: Offline text statistics CLI
source_request: Build a small command-line tool that reports useful statistics for a UTF-8 text file.
requirements: Expose a Python package textstats with python -m textstats PATH --json as the command-line entry point.
For a readable UTF-8 file, print one JSON object containing lines, words, characters, and unique_words as non-negative integers.
Count lines with str.splitlines(), characters with len(text), and words with Unicode-aware non-whitespace tokenization; unique_words counts casefolded distinct words.
For missing files and invalid UTF-8, exit nonzero with a useful stderr message and no JSON success output.
Provide automated pytest coverage and a README with installation, usage, tests, and limitations.

acceptance_criteria.description: The CLI produces exactly the specified JSON counts for UTF-8 inputs, including empty and Unicode text.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_ACCEPTANCE against the isolated snapshot.

acceptance_criteria.description: Missing paths and invalid UTF-8 fail with actionable stderr and no success JSON.
acceptance_criteria.verification: Run CHECK_ACCEPTANCE against the isolated snapshot.

acceptance_criteria.description: The package compiles, passes Ruff and its own pytest suite, and contains a usable README.

constraints: Use Python 3.12 and the standard library for the runtime tool.
Keep source, tests, and documentation inside the supplied Git repository.
Do not require network access, credentials, or a hosted service at runtime.
assumptions: A path names one local regular file and input files are small enough to read into memory.
